stageContracts.description:
## Layer 2: self-injective modules, total acyclicity, and singularities

For a finite-dimensional `k`-algebra `A` that is self-injective on both sides, put the ordinary
abelian exact structure on finite-dimensional right `A`-modules. Prove that it is Frobenius and
that its projective-injectives are exactly the finite-dimensional projective modules. Every
finite-dimensional Frobenius algebra satisfies these self-injectivity hypotheses. Symmetric
Frobenius algebras form an important special case, not every Frobenius algebra.
Construct `stmod-A` and its triangulation. Keep it distinct from the quotient of the category of
all modules, usually written `StMod-A`.

For a left-and-right noetherian ring `R`, define a totally acyclic complex of finitely generated
projective right modules: every term is finitely generated and projective, the complex is acyclic,
and `Hom_R(P,R)` is acyclic. Finite generation is a condition on every term of the complex, not a
consequence of finite generation of one cycle: adding a contractible two-term disk on an infinite
free module away from degree zero preserves acyclicity, dual acyclicity, and the degree-zero cycle.
Define finitely generated Gorenstein-projective right modules as degree-zero cycles in such
complexes. Prove that this definition is independent of the chosen complete resolution and build:

- the exact Frobenius category `Gproj-R`, with the exact structure inherited from finitely
  generated modules;
- projective-injective objects exactly the finitely generated projective modules;
- the stable equivalence between `Gproj-R` and the homotopy category of totally acyclic complexes
  of finitely generated projectives, by cycle and complete-resolution functors.

An **Iwanaga–Gorenstein ring** here means left and right noetherian with both self-injective
dimensions finite. Under precisely that hypothesis, define

`D_sg(R) = D^b(mod-R) / K^b(proj-R)`

as a Verdier quotient and prove Buchweitz's triangle equivalence
`stable(Gproj-R) ≃ D_sg(R)`. Give both the stalk/cokernel functor and the complete-resolution
quasi-inverse. State all left/right noetherian and finite self-injective-dimension assumptions in
the theorem, not in prose or ambient namespaces.

Specialize:

- if `R` is a finite-dimensional self-injective algebra, every finite-dimensional right module
  is Gorenstein-projective, so `stmod-R ≃ D_sg(R)`;
- if `R` is left/right noetherian of finite global dimension, `D_sg(R)` is zero;
- for an essentially small Frobenius exact category `E`, construct the Keller–Vossieck
  Example 2.3 comparison from `Stable E` to the exact-derived quotient
  `D^b(E)/K^b(ProjInj E)` and prove it is a triangle equivalence. Here `D^b(E)` is the bounded
  derived category of the specified Quillen exact structure. Supply a separate
  idempotent-completion compatibility theorem when `E` is idempotent complete; do not replace
  `D^b(E)` by `K^b(E)`—that analogous quotient need not be equivalent.

The second bullet is not a claim that the stable category of an arbitrary ring of finite global
dimension is zero. The self-injective specialization and the finite-global-dimension
specialization are different hypotheses.

independentReviewAudit.ownership: Read every original cited stage contract and reviewed coverage row, and independently searched both pinned libraries and the refreshed atlas corpus for every input item. Generic Koszul complexes coalesce at DD.1; IHG.6 is a consumer. Complete resolutions/Buchweitz comparison import StablePeriodicCurved layer 2. Generic local duality and the additional local-ring Tate sequence remain ownership gaps. The now accepted CG routes 1 and 3 are proposal imports, not fabricated built stages.

previous.statement: O is a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer ϖ. For an O-module U, tors(U) is its torsion submodule and U^tf := U/tors(U) its torsion-free quotient, giving the exact sequence 0 → tors(U) → U → U^tf → 0, functorial in U. When U is finitely generated, U^tf is finite free, so the sequence splits (non-functorially); hence for any additive functor E on finitely generated O-modules, E(U) → E(U^tf) is surjective. For a map α: U → V the induced map Coker α → Coker(α^tf) is surjective (so α onto implies α^tf onto), and if Ker α is torsion then α^tf is injective.
previous.note: The defining objects are in Mathlib: tors(U) is `Submodule.torsion O U` (elements killed by a non-zero-divisor), U^tf is `U ⧸ torsion O U`, which is torsion-free, and it is free when U is finitely generated over the DVR (a PID). The splitting comes from `Module.projective_lifting_property`; Mathlib's structure theorem over a PID uses exactly this splitting. Mathlib does not state the induced map α^tf, the surjectivity of E(U) → E(U^tf) for additive E, or the two remarks (Coker α ↠ Coker α^tf; Ker α torsion ⇒ α^tf injective). These are short consequences (`Submodule.mapQ`, once linear maps are shown to preserve torsion), and whichever layer builds F^i_A (item F-functor) must supply them.

previous.statement: A is a noetherian local ring and λ_A: A → O a surjective local homomorphism onto the discrete valuation ring O. Set p_A := Ker(λ_A), a prime ideal, and c := height p_A (the codimension; c = dim A_{p_A}). Then dim A ≥ height p_A + dim(A/p_A) = c + 1; no restriction is placed on dim A.
previous.note: The setting of 2.2 needs no new definition. It consists of a Noetherian local A, a surjective local hom to a DVR (`IsDiscreteValuationRing`, `IsLocalHom`), p_A = ker (prime by `RingHom.ker_isPrime`) and c = `Ideal.height` p_A, which equals dim A_p by `IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height`. The inequality dim A ≥ height p + dim A/p = c + 1 is not stated in ring form. It follows from the order-theoretic `krullDim = ⨆ (height + coheight)` together with `ringKrullDim_quotient` / `Order.coheight_eq_krullDim_Ici` (and dim O = 1), a short bridge that the consumer writes. Mathlib bundles no 'augmented local ring' structure; the category C_O is a separate item (category-CO).

previous.statement: The cotangent module of λ_A is the finitely generated O-module p_A/p_A². Its torsion submodule is Φ_A := tors(p_A/p_A²) (2.8). When c = 0 and A is regular at p_A, Φ_A = p_A/p_A².
previous.note: The cotangent module p_A/p_A² is `Ideal.Cotangent p_A`, a module over A ⧸ p_A. That ring is identified with O by `RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective` λ_A, and Φ_A is its `Submodule.torsion`. The remark that Φ_A = p/p² when c = 0 and A is regular at p_A is a consequence of Lemma 2.7, which is missing.

previous.statement: (§2, p. 16) C_O is the category of pairs (A, λ_A) where A is a complete noetherian local ring and λ_A: A → O is a surjective local homomorphism with A regular at p_A := Ker(λ_A), i.e. A_{p_A} is a regular local ring. The paper says only that the morphisms are 'the obvious ones'; in later use (e.g. 7.1) a morphism φ: (A, λ_A) → (B, λ_B) is a local homomorphism with λ_B ∘ φ = λ_A. Completeness is imposed 'only for ease of exposition, especially in Section 5 and beyond'. One often speaks of the ring A being in C_O. C_O(c) is the subcategory of C_O of those A with height p_A = c, equivalently rank_O(p_A/p_A²) = c (Lemma 2.7). (The Introduction, p. 4, and the Glossary, p. 80, describe the narrower class of pairs with A a complete local noetherian O-algebra (in CNL_O) and λ a surjective O-algebra map; the Introduction says the text treats a larger class.)
previous.note: No library or layer defines the category of pairs (A, λ_A: A ↠ O) with A complete Noetherian local and A_{p_A} regular, or its subcategories C_O(c). DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1 plans the coefficient categories C_Λ and Ĉ_Λ, objects with a residue-field identification. That is a near miss: it has no augmentation to O and no regularity at p_A. See sourceIssues E23: the §2 definition must require O-algebras.

Missing. The item uses the corrected statement (sourceIssues E4): the equality 'iff length Φ_A = length Φ_B' needs M_{p_B} ≠ 0. The proof needs depth, Ext vanishing against m-power-torsion complexes (Rees in Mathlib covers only the module case), the isomorphism of regular local rings A_{p_A} ≅ B_{p_B}, and Proposition 6.10 (C3). None of these is in the libraries as a congruence-module statement. For c = 0 this is Brochard–Iyengar–Khare [12, Lemma 3.4]. See sourceIssues E4.

The maps π₁ = [K 1 L] and π₂ = [K diag(ϖ_v,1) L] are ALS.3 change-of-level double-coset operators, which is planned. The level-lowering map π_{K,v}, its adjoint for ϕ_K, and the identity π_{K,v} ∘ U_v = (T_v −1; Nm(v) 0) ∘ π_{K,v} are planned nowhere for PGL₂/F; the analogous degeneracy maps appear only for modular curves (ModularCurvesPartII R14.1). The identity is a computation in the mixed-level Hecke module H(K\G/L), which Tau Ceti's HeckeCosetModule.mul could host once the coset decompositions in PGL₂(F_v) exist. See sourceIssues E53.

Missing. The Koszul complex as a chain complex is planned (DD.1, IHG.6), but the DG-algebra structure and the Tate construction A⟨X,Y⟩ with its independence of choices are not. Misprint E5 applies: z_i = Σ_j (u_ij + g′_ij) x_j, as the item states. See sourceIssues E5.

previous.statement: Let R be a Gorenstein local ring, M ∈ mod R (finitely generated) a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R-module, and x ∈ R not a zero-divisor on R and on M (x lies in the maximal ideal in every application, and the Nakayama step of the proof uses this). If the R/xR-module M/xM has a free summand of rank µ, then so does the R-module M.
previous.note: This lifts free summands from M/xM to M for an MCM module over a Gorenstein local ring, using the trace-ideal criterion, Nakayama and Ext^1_R(M,R) = 0 from (9.1). Neither library has Gorenstein rings, MCM modules or the trace criterion. Generic ingredients exist: Nakayama, contractLeft, and IsSMulRegular short exact sequences in ModuleCat. No layer plans it.

previous.statement: (Assumed.) Let K = ∏_v K_v ⊆ PGL_2(A_F^∞) be compact open and S a finite set of places with K_v maximal compact in PGL_2(F_v) for v ∉ S. (i) For every maximal ideal m of T^S(K) there is a semisimple ρ̄_m: G_F → GL_2(T^S(K)/m) such that for all v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄_m|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and ρ̄_m(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). (ii) There is a lift ρ_K: G_F → GL_2(T^S(K)_m) of ρ̄_m such that for all v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, ρ_K|_{G_{F_v}} is unramified and ρ_K(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). For F CM, (i) is known by Scholze's work and (ii) for sufficiently large ℓ ([45, Theorems 1.1, 1.3]); this is similar to [17, Conjecture A]. Remark 13.3: suppose ρ̄_m is irreducible. Then (ii) follows from a weaker assumption: for some T ∈ CNL_O with an inclusion T^S(K)_m ↪ T there is a lift ρ_K: G_F → GL_2(T) of ρ̄_m that is unramified at every v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ, with ρ_K(Frob_v) of characteristic polynomial x² − T_v x + Nm(v). The reason is Chebotarev: the traces of Frob_v (v ∉ S, v ∤ ℓ) lie in T^S(K)_m.
previous.note: Conjecture A is an open hypothesis for general F, and no layer states or proves it, not even for CM fields. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds the infrastructure of Scholze's argument but says it is 'not an additional requirement to formalize its final Galois-representation theorem'. IHG.5 gives determinant schemas modulo nilpotent ideals, AG2 covers characteristic zero only, and the Newton–Thorne removal of the nilpotent ideal for large ℓ (part (ii), from Newton–Thorne 2016) is planned nowhere; the atlas's NEWTON-THORNE source is the symmetric-power papers. Remark 13.3 (a lift over a larger T descends to T^S(K)_m) is covered by IHG.1's reconstruction over complete local rings under residual absolute irreducibility, together with Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev layer 10).

previous.name: Theorem G: integral R = T for Bianchi manifolds assuming Conjecture B
previous.statement: Standing assumption (Introduction p. 6): ℓ is unramified in F. Let F be an imaginary quadratic field and assume Conjecture B holds for F. Let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T(K_0(N_∅)) such that N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅ and ρ̄_m|_{G_{F(ζ_ℓ)}} is absolutely irreducible. For ℓ > 20 there exists an integer µ ≥ 1 such that for all Σ (Σ ⊆ T as in §13) there is an isomorphism of R_Σ-modules H_1(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ} ≅ R_Σ^µ ⊕ W_Σ for some R_Σ-module W_Σ. In particular, R_Σ acts faithfully on H_1(Y_0(N_Σ), O)_{m_Σ}, and so the map R_Σ ↠ T_Σ from Conjecture B is an isomorphism for all Σ. (This is deduced from Theorem F. Conjecture A holds by Newton–Thorne [45, Theorem 1.3] for ℓ sufficiently large, and ℓ > 20 suffices when [F:Q] = 2 (footnote 1, citing [45, (1.2)]). Conjecture C holds because Y_K is a 3-manifold and H_i(Y_K, k)_m = 0 for i = 0, 3 when m is non-Eisenstein. Conjecture D is Theorem 13.12, which needs ℓ > 3.)
previous.note: This is Theorem F for imaginary quadratic F. Conjecture A comes from Newton–Thorne [45, Thm 1.3] (ℓ > 20), Conjecture C is automatic for 3-manifolds and Conjecture D is Theorem 13.12; the theorem remains conditional on Conjecture B. The atlas plans neither Bianchi R = T nor Newton–Thorne's torsion Galois representations in the derived category: TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds the library under Scholze's theorem but 'not … its final Galois-representation theorem', and ACC+'s nilpotent-ideal local–global compatibility is infrastructure only. Neither library has anything. See sourceIssues E64: the cited Newton–Thorne theorems do not give Conjecture A(ii) for trivial coefficients.

previous.statement: Remark 12.2. In the main results (e.g. Theorem 15.1), (non-minimal) ramification of lifts of ρ̄ is allowed only at the places of Proposition 12.1 whose eigenvalue ratio is q_v. These are the 'level raising' primes: v ∤ ℓ, ρ̄_v unramified, q_v ≢ 1 (mod ℓ), and ρ̄_v(Frob_v) has eigenvalue ratio q_v. The restriction is made mainly for simplicity. The authors expect, without proof, that one could also treat without much trouble (i) unrestricted ramification at places v with q_v ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), ρ̄ unramified at v and ρ̄(Frob_v) having distinct eigenvalues, and (ii) unipotent ramification at places v with q_v ≡ 1 (mod ℓ), ρ̄ unramified at v and ρ̄(Frob_v) of order divisible by ℓ. Unipotent ramification at places trivial for ρ̄ would need more work. As printed, the Remark also claims: (a) if ρ̄ is odd at a real place of F with complex conjugation c ∈ G_F, then any v with ρ̄(Frob_v) conjugate to ρ̄(c) is a level raising prime, with q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ); (b) if the projective image of ρ̄ is PSL_2(k) (|k| ≥ 5) and [F(ζ_ℓ):F] > 2, then there are places v with ρ̄(Frob_v) having eigenvalue ratio q_v and q_v ≢ ±1 (mod ℓ), and these are again level raising primes. Correction (sourceIssues E41, E42): (a) holds when det ρ̄ = ε̄_ℓ (e.g. Case (PGL2)); in general one must add the hypothesis q_v ≡ −1 (mod ℓ), i.e. Frob_v conjugate to c in Gal(F(ρ̄, ζ_ℓ)/F). (b) holds when ℓ ≥ 7 or [k:F_ℓ] is even, with k the field over which the projective image is PSL_2(k). It fails for ℓ = 5 with [k:F_5] odd. The Remark gives no proofs and is not used in later proofs.
previous.note: No layer plans existence of level-raising primes (v∤ℓ, ρ̄ unramified at v, q_v ≢ 1, eigenvalue ratio q_v) over a general number field. GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5 chooses only Taylor–Wiles primes (q ≡ 1 mod p^n). The closest special case is KW I Lemma 8.2 in the ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.4 decomposition node: over Q, with p ≡ 1 mod 4, non-solvable image and q ≡ −1 mod p. The inputs are planned elsewhere: Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev, layers 10 and 14, not built) and the GL2/PGL2 image facts (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4). Possible source error: the first sentence is true when det ρ̄ = ε̄_ℓ (Case (PGL2)) but not for general ψ. For example, in Case (Wt1) take the level-23 weight-one S3 form with ℓ = 5 and v = 11, which is inert in Q(√−23) and ≡ 1 mod 5: then ρ̄(Frob_11) ~ ρ̄(c), but q_v ≡ 1. One needs Frob_v ~ c in Gal(F(ρ̄,ζ_ℓ)/F). See sourceIssues E41, E42.

previous.statement: Assume Conjecture A; fix a non-Eisenstein m ⊆ T^S(K_0(N_∅)) with N(ρ̄_m) = N_∅. For compact open K ⊆ K_0(N_∅) there is a natural derived T(K)_m-isomorphism (C_K)_m ≅ RHom_O((C_K)_m, O)[2r_1 + 3r_2] = (C_K)_m^† in D_{T(K)_m}(O); the adjoint of [K_2αK_1]: (C_{K_1})_m → (C_{K_2})_m is [K_1α^{−1}K_2]. (Newton–Thorne [45, Prop. 3.7, Thm 4.2].)
previous.note: ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans Poincaré–Lefschetz/Verdier duality for perfect complexes with Hecke adjoint formulas; its contract says 'Hecke adjoints use inverse double cosets'. ALS.4 plans the boundary triangle and boundary vanishing after localization 'by an actual eigenvalue argument'; that step identifies homology with Borel–Moore homology at non-Eisenstein m, and is Newton–Thorne's condition ♠ (Conjecture A for GL₂, class field theory for GL₁). Neither library has any of this. A possible gap (not in issues_draft, not checked against Newton–Thorne 2016, which treats CM fields): if F has a real place, Y_K can be non-orientable. For F = ℚ, t = 5, (7 2; 25 7) ∈ PGL₂(ℚ) ∩ K₁(25) has det −1 and infinite order, so duality pairs C_K with the orientation-twisted complex, and the Poincaré pairing vanishes on H₁(Ỹ)⁺ = H₁(Y_K); a fix is K∞° or an orientation twist. See sourceIssues E65 (orientation at real places).

previous.statement: Let r, ℓ_0 and j be the integers of 10.1, 10.3 and 10.4, and let PaSy be the category of patching systems over (Λ_n) (for fixed d, ℓ_0). Let R∞ be a complete local, flat, noetherian O-algebra of dimension r + j − ℓ_0 + 1 (so ℓ_0 = dim S∞ − dim R∞), equipped with surjective O-algebra morphisms π_n: R∞ ↠ R_n^□ for n ≥ 1, not assumed compatible. Then there is a homomorphism ϕ∞: S∞ → R∞ making R∞ a finite S∞-algebra, and a functor P: PaSy → mod R∞, such that: (1) P(C) is a maximal Cohen–Macaulay R∞-module, nonzero when C ≠ 0. (2) There is a surjection R∞/nR∞ ↠ R_0 and an isomorphism of R_0-modules P(C)/nP(C) ≅ H_d(C_0). (3) Treating P(C) as an S∞-module via ϕ∞: for any open ideal a ⊆ S∞ and for infinitely many n, there are isomorphisms (S∞/a) ⊗^L_{S∞} P(C)[d] ≅ (S∞/a) ⊗^L_{Λ_n^□} C_n^□ of derived R∞-complexes, where R∞ acts on C_n^□ via ι_n^□ π_n (ι_n: R_n → End_{D(Λ_n)}(C_n) is the derived action of 10.3(3)). (4) There is an isomorphism of R∞-algebras End_{D(S∞)}(P(C)) ≅ lim_a End_{D(S∞/a)}((S∞/a) ⊗^L_{S∞} P(C)). (5) Fix a map f: C → C in PaSy. If there is τ ∈ R∞ with π_n(τ) = f_n^□ as elements of End_{D(Λ_n^□)}(C_n^□) for all but finitely many n, then P(f) = τ in End_{R∞}(P(C)). (The proof shows that in (3) the set of good n lies in the ultrafilter F. The misprint 'proving (2)' at the end of the proof of (3) is E17.)
previous.note: P8 plans this theorem, and its ACC+ §6.4 node covers parts (2)–(5); P9's codimension–amplitude lemma gives part (1). One step has no named layer: choosing ϕ∞ so that R∞ is finite over S∞, which adapts Böckle–Khare–Manning [8, Lemmas 3.6–3.7]; R03.4 is the nearest owner. The functoriality step the paper 'leave[s] to the reader' (homotopies are preserved) must be written out. The draft statement drops the framing: on p. 43, π_n: R∞ ↠ R_n^□, and parts (3) and (5) read ⊗^L_{Λ_n^□} C_n^□, ι_n^□ π_n and f_n^□ ∈ End_{D(Λ_n^□)}(C_n^□). Gaps in the proof: sourceIssues E34 (finiteness of R∞ over S∞), E35 (finiteness of R_n in 10.1), E17 (misprint).

previous.statement: (i) For every maximal ideal m of T^S(K) there is a semisimple ρ̄_m: G_Q → GL_2(T^S(K)/m), unramified at v ∉ S, v ≠ ℓ, with tr ρ̄_m(Frob_v) = T_v mod m, and unramified at ℓ. (ii) There is a lift ρ_K: G_Q → GL_2(T^S(K)_m), unramified at v ∉ S ∪ {ℓ} with char. poly x² − T_v x + ψ(Frob_v) (ψ the Teichmüller lift of det ρ̄_m), and unramified at ℓ. (Proof: the doubling method of Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11], with injectivity of the doubling map proved without q-expansions via Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni [10, §5.1].)
previous.note: No layer plans the doubling argument, for modular or for Shimura curves: Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11], with the q-expansion-free injectivity through the supersingular locus of [10, §5.1]. The partial inputs are AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2 (quaternionic and Hilbert Galois representations in cohomological weight), R19.6 (determinant law and representation over a localised Hecke algebra) and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.4 (determinants through finite quotients). R19.1 and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.5 give Deligne–Serre in characteristic zero, which does not reach torsion weight-one Hecke algebras or unramifiedness at ℓ. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.1 only 'Organize[s] Deligne-Serre Artin representations, weight-one modularity in proved cases'. See sourceIssues E57 (the determinant at Taylor–Wiles level) and E16 (misprint).

previous.statement: For any Σ ⊆ T, any Q, and 𝔇, the representations ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}: G_Q → GL_2(T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) from Theorem 14.5 (with K = K^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) arise from the universal representation G_Q → GL_2(R^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) via surjections R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}. The printed text reads 'ρ^𝔇_Σ: G_F → GL_2(T^𝔇_Σ)', a misprint (sourceIssues E61); see also E57 on the determinant at Taylor–Wiles level. These satisfy: (1) tr ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}(Frob_v) = T_v for all v ∉ S. (2) There is a natural O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure on T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}, defined as in §13 via the full Hecke algebra, which makes R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} an O[Δ_Q]-algebra homomorphism. (3) For v ∈ Σ, let B_v ∈ T_Σ^{𝔇,□} be the image of B_v ∈ R_v^{uni(ε_v)} under R_v^{uni(ε_v)} ↪ R_{Σ,loc} → R_Σ^□ ↠ T_Σ^{𝔇,□} (printed with R_v^□). Then (B_v) = (ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1}) U_v − 1) as ideals of T_Σ^{𝔇,□}. (4) For Σ_1 ⊆ Σ_2 ⊆ T the following squares commute: R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} over R^𝔇_Σ → T^𝔇_Σ, and R^𝔇_{Σ_2,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ_2,Q} over R^𝔇_{Σ_1,Q} → T^𝔇_{Σ_1,Q}. Proof: a variant of the doubling method used for Theorem 14.5.
previous.note: This is Conjecture B in weight one: surjections R^𝔇_{Σ,Q} ↠ T^𝔇_{Σ,Q} with trace compatibility, the O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure, the ideal condition (B_v) = (ε_v√(q_vψ(ϕ_v)^{−1})U_v − 1) at v ∈ Σ, and compatibility in Σ and Q. GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 plans deformation-to-Hecke maps only for weight ≥ 2 Betti/étale Hecke algebras. Nothing plans them for weight-one coherent Hecke algebras. The printed statement has ρ^𝔇_Σ: G_F → GL_2(T^𝔇_Σ) where ρ^𝔇_{Σ,Q}: G_Q → GL_2(T^𝔇_{Σ,Q}) is meant (misprint, affects nothing). See sourceIssues E57, E61.

No layer plans the self-duality ϕ_K = (Proposition 13.6) ∘ w_K, twisted by the Atkin–Lehner operators w_v = [K(0 −1; ϖ_v 0)K] at Iwahori/K₁(v) level, or the adjoint formula w_{K₁}[K₁α⁻¹K₂]w_{K₂}. ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans only the untwisted inverse-double-coset adjoint. Tau Ceti's Atkin–Lehner material concerns Γ₀(N) ⊂ GL₂(ℚ) acting on modular forms, and the anti-involution used for commutativity of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring; that is a near miss. The matrix identities used (w_v normalizes K_v; w(a 0; 0 d)⁻¹w⁻¹ = (a 0; 0 d) in PGL₂(F_v)) are routine; the item inherits the orientation caveat of prop-13-6. See sourceIssues E50, E51.

The proposition gives the self-duality ϕ_{Σ,Q} of the Taylor–Wiles complexes, compatible with ⊗ᴸ_{O[Δ_Q]} O, and the level-raising identities π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ U_v² − 1 ≃ π_v^† ∘ π_v up to units, which is Ribet's computation (Ribet 1984, Proposition 3.3) transported to complexes. It is not planned. Level change and level raising are planned only for modular curves (ModularCurvesPartII R14.1, R14.4) and Shimura curves (R18.4, 'degeneracy-map properties'). The item builds on the missing Proposition 13.7, the level-lowering maps and T_{Σ,Q}, and inherits the orientation caveat of prop-13-6. See sourceIssues E53.
The duality functor of §13 (p. 58); the shift 2r_1+3r_2 = 2d + ℓ_0 matches 11.2. Missing; ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans Verdier duality of the complexes but not this normalization.

Abstract patching (P8) and the depth and amplitude conclusions (P9) are planned, and PA.4 plans the analogous 'is a patching system' check for the ACC+ tower. No layer plans compatibility of patching with Grothendieck duality (Theorem 11.3) or the arithmetic self-duality 𝔆_Σ^† ≅ 𝔆_Σ, which comes from Props. 13.6, 13.7 and 13.9, or from Prop. 14.7. ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.5:finite-level-duality plans only the finite-level Poincaré–Verdier duality that feeds Prop. 13.6. The printed 𝔆_Σ^∨ should be the dual patching system 𝔆_Σ^† (E12). See sourceIssues E12.

The finite-level inputs belong to other clusters: the formulas π_v∘π_v^† = U_v² − 1 (Prop. 13.10) or q_vU_v² − ψ(φ_v) (Prop. 14.7), Conjecture D via Lemma 13.11 or Prop. 14.8, and Conjecture B(3)/Theorem 14.6(3). No atlas layer plans patched level-lowering maps, their surjectivity by Nakayama, or the identities π_v∘π_v^∨ = u_vB_v and π_v^∨∘π_v = u′_vB_v in R_{T,∞}. The nearest plans are ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 (Ihara's lemma on modular curves), SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 (old/new sequences and congruence modules at finite level) and P9 (derived Ihara avoidance, the opposite strategy). See sourceIssues E55.

This is the Wiles/Diamond induction on the level, run on the patched modules. It rests on the numerical criterion (Theorems 9.2 and 9.5), the change of congruence modules (Prop. 4.4) and invariance of domain (Theorem 7.4), all from the paper's commutative-algebra clusters, and no atlas layer plans a numerical-criterion or free-summand argument for patched modules. The nearest plans are GL2ModularityLifting R22.4 (non-minimal levels, integral R = T) and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.6. Both follow KW II and Calegari–Geraghty support and component arguments, not congruence modules, and have ℓ₀ = 0 or characteristic-zero conclusions. Neither library has anything.

The theorem follows from Theorem 15.4 by specialising along S_∞ → O. Only the surjection R_{Σ,∞}/n ↠ R_Σ is justified in the paper (gap E13), but that surjection suffices for the conclusion. GL2ModularityLifting R22.4 plans non-minimal levels and an integral R = T strengthening, but for the KW II setting: ℓ₀ = 0 and Hilbert or quaternionic modules. No layer plans R = T for the torsion homology of PGL₂/F arithmetic manifolds (Case PGL2) or for weight-one coherent cohomology of Shimura curves (Case Wt1, Theorem H). Neither library has any R = T statement. The isomorphism R_{Σ,∞} ⊗_{S∞} O ≅ R_Σ asserted before Theorem 15.4 is only a consequence (sourceIssues E13).

This is Case (PGL2) of Theorem 15.1, conditional on Conjectures A, B, C and D, with the Introduction's extra hypothesis ℓ > 3. No atlas layer states conditional R = T theorems for PGL₂ over an arbitrary number field. The conjectural inputs themselves are the cluster C7 items. Neither library has anything. For F with a real place see sourceIssues E65.

This is the coherent analogue of Proposition 13.10. It needs the Serre-duality self-duality at Taylor–Wiles level (compatible with ⊗^L_{O[Δ_Q]} O) and the identity π_v ∘ π_v^† ≃ q_vU_v² − ψ(ϕ_v), both ways round, for the coherent level-lowering maps. The (−)^† and adjoint formalism is algebra in the paper's §§10–11 (other clusters). The geometric duality and the degeneracy-map computation on weight-one coherent cohomology are planned nowhere; HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.4 plans degeneracy maps only for Betti/étale cohomology.

This is Theorem H, the main weight-one integral R = T theorem on Shimura curves. No layer plans an integral R = T for weight-one coherent cohomology: GL2ModularityLifting R22.x covers weight ≥ 2 Betti/étale settings, and ML.1 only registers 'weight-one modularity in proved cases'. Correction to the draft: as printed (p. 8, Theorem H; pp. 72–73), T^𝔇_Σ acts on the cohomology H^1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O)_m, which the paper identifies with H^0(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_{E/O})^*, i.e. H_0(C^𝔇_Σ). The draft's H_1(X^𝔇_Σ, ω_O) is by Serre duality the torsion-free H^0(X, ω_O), which is a different module.

This is Theorem I, the torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence in weight one. It combines Theorem 14.9 and Calegari's 𝔇 = ∅ theorem (calegari-wt1) with three planned inputs: classical Jacquet–Langlands (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3), level and weight optimisation (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2/R20.3) and companion forms (item companion-forms, partly planned). It also uses the vanishing H^1(X_O, ω^{⊗ℓ}) = 0 for ℓ > 2, via Serre duality and Kodaira–Spencer. The torsion correspondence itself is planned nowhere. As printed (pp. 8, 73–74) the Hecke algebras act on H^1(X, ω_O), not the H_1 of the draft.
The Introduction's stated consequence (p. 7) of Theorems F and G. A torsion ρ must satisfy the local conditions defining R_Σ for the conclusion to apply. Missing.

No layer plans any of three things: the ℓ-integral weight-one sheaf ω_A = e·π_*Ω_{𝒜/𝒳_{K,A}} on a quaternionic Shimura curve (with the Diamond–Taylor idempotent e = e^*), the Pontryagin-dual coherent homology H_i(X, ω_O) := lim Hom_O(H^i(X, ω_{O/ϖ^n}), E/O), or the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω on the Shimura curve. The nearest layers do less. AutomorphicBundles B2/B4 work in characteristic zero over canonical models, with explicit weights only for GL₂, Hilbert, Siegel and unitary PEL. AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1 covers the Hodge bundle and Kodaira–Spencer on modular curves only, per its reviewed decomposition node. AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 ('identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration') and PELModuli M6 ('universal abelian scheme and its Hodge line') are generic ingredients. Tau Ceti defines only the groups Hⁱ(X, M).

The geometric input is not planned: Čech complexes of ω_{O/ϖ^n} for the étale Galois cover X_{K_Δ} → X_K (group Δ), giving perfect (O/ϖ^n)[Δ]-complexes with the stated base-change isomorphisms and amplitude [0,1] mod ϖ. Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layers B–C and StableReduction Layer 2 plan the ingredients: Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme, vanishing above degree one on a curve, and base change over a locally Noetherian base. The algebraic step from the compatible system to a perfect O[Δ]-complex (Khare–Thorne [38, Lemmas 2.13–2.14]) falls within DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7. The Δ-equivariant construction on the Shimura curve is planned nowhere. See sourceIssues E58.

Serre duality itself is planned in Tau Ceti roadmaps: JacobianChallenge Layer B over a field, and the shared 'J-B / SR-2' relative dualizing-sheaf interface of StableReduction Layer 2 for proper flat Gorenstein curves over a locally Noetherian base (hence over O and O/ϖ^n). Not planned is the derived, T^S(K)-equivariant self-duality C_K^𝔇 ≅ RHom_O(C_K^𝔇, O)[1]. That also needs the Shimura-curve Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω and the behaviour of the Hecke correspondences under duality (Boxer–Pilloni [11, §3.2]). Neither library has a dualizing sheaf or Serre duality. See sourceIssues E59.

Proposition 14.2 is Proposition 14.3 combined with Lemma 10.8 (item lemma-10-8, cluster C5); Proposition 14.3 is missing, so this is missing too. IHG.2 plans the comparison of derived and cohomological Hecke actions only up to a nilpotent ('ghost') ideal. That is strictly weaker than faithfulness on H_0 and does not identify T^S(K) with the classical Hecke algebra on H^0(X, ω_{E/O}). The paper prints H^0(C_K^𝔇) in cohomological indexing, which is H_0 in the homological indexing of Proposition 14.1.

No layer constructs the double-coset operators T_v, U_v, ⟨d⟩_v on the integral coherent complexes C_K^𝔇 of a Shimura curve, or the algebra T^S(K) ⊆ End_{D(O)}(C_K^𝔇). HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.2 ('prove extension of Hecke maps') and AutomorphicBundles B5 (Hecke pullback and trace on automorphic bundles over canonical models) supply pieces. So do IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.2 (image algebras of a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex; sole owner per RS-24) and P7 (Hecke actions through inverse limits, cf. [38, §2.4]). Mathlib's abstract HeckeRing is a near miss: it is a double-coset convolution ring, not an action on any complex. See sourceIssues E56.

Hasse invariants are planned only in three other settings: modular curves (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.3, via q-expansions), Hilbert–Blumenthal ordinary loci (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2), and Ekedahl–Oort strata in the Igusa/perfectoid setting (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2). None constructs Ha ∈ H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗(ℓ−1)}) on a quaternionic Shimura curve over Q with simple zeros exactly at the supersingular points. None proves its Hecke equivariance (T_r and U_r for r ≠ ℓ; U_ℓ in weight ≥ 2), Kassaei's lift H̃a for ℓ > 3, or that H̃a^{ℓ^{m−1}} mod ϖ^m is independent of the lift and Hecke-equivariant (Boxer [9, Prop. 7.2.1]). The reviewed audit (AUDIT-13) finds no Hasse invariant in either library.
Weight-one analogue of Proposition 13.9 and of the construction of π_v in 13.6 (14.2, p. 72), with (−)^† := RHom_O(−, O)[1], d = 0, ℓ_0 = 1 (14.1, p. 68). Missing.

The one step where the Shimura-curve proof of Theorem 14.5 differs from Calegari–Geraghty [17, Thm 3.11]: q-expansions are replaced by restriction to the supersingular locus as in Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni [10, §5.1]. Missing.

Links the main theorems (stated for H^1(X, ω_O)) with the machinery (H_0(C_K^𝔇)). Serre duality over a field is planned in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge layer B; this integral Pontryagin-dual form on Shimura curves is not.

Calegari [16] (J. Reine Angew. Math. 740 (2018), 41–62) proves R^∅_Σ ≅ T^∅_Σ in weight one on modular curves for ℓ > 3. He uses q-expansions to show the patched module is free over the patched Hecke algebra. No layer plans it: ML.1's 'weight-one modularity in proved cases' is a registry that names no such source, and AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1–R15.3 plan only the Katz-form and q-expansion inputs on modular curves. The Hecke module is H^1(X^∅_Σ, ω_O)_m (printed H^1), not the H_1 of the draft.

sourceIssueChanges: All 65 receive independent verdicts; E42 rejected. E34/E35/E55/E57/E64/E65 narrowed as recorded in priorReviewFields. Original search claims preserved separately.

gaps.title: Cited-source closure and granularity
gaps.detail: The 40 bibliography prerequisite requests are retained. Only the bounded supporting portions listed below were independently read. Lescot, Grothendieck local duality, Buchweitz’s precise Tate norm sequence, full DG Γ/acyclic-closure theory, quasi-complete intersections, FKR, Gross/Coleman–Voloch, Khare–Thorne and the quaternionic doubling suppliers are not a completed proof DAG. Split bundled multipart input claims when completing that DAG.

gaps.title: Generic local duality ownership
gaps.detail: R03.3 plans depth/CM/AB/CI, but its read contract does not explicitly provide normalized dualizing complexes and Grothendieck local duality in the generality of §4. A0-extension and coherent-curve duality are adjacent geometric suppliers, not automatically this ring theorem. Establish the unique generic owner and precise extension before route 3 can be activated.

gaps.title: Local-ring Tate cohomology ownership
gaps.detail: StablePeriodicCurved layer 2 already owns complete resolutions, total acyclicity and the Buchweitz comparison. Build on it; do not replan it. The local-ring Tate cohomology/norm exact sequence used here needs an explicit supplier contract or Part II. Finite-group Tate cohomology and finite-group/sheaf Tate proposals are different notions.

gaps.title: Patching finiteness
gaps.detail: E34/E35 require one joint proof: construct the coefficient map for the whole functor and justify the hypotheses used in its finiteness argument without assuming global R finite over O before R=T. The extractor’s dim Qbar equality and unchanged-proof assertion were withdrawn. The full Theorem 10.6 bundle is now missing, with existing P7–P9 subcomponents imported.

gaps.title: Weight-one determinant and Hecke transport
gaps.detail: E57 needs an actual fixed-determinant/diamond convention and its compatibility with traces, levels, covering groups, duality and deformation-to-Hecke maps. A scalar twist changes traces. Perfectness does not imply free H₀. Import the accepted CG defect-one and coherent-complex proposals, then prove the additional Shimura adapters.

gaps.title: All-level scalar identities
gaps.detail: E55 requires U_v membership and B_v–U_v scalar identities with compatible units at every auxiliary Q_n, before patching. Neither Q=∅ ideal equality nor reduction modulo the augmentation gives this.

gaps.title: Integral Galois representation for trivial coefficients
gaps.detail: For Theorem G keep nilpotent-free Conjecture A(ii). The cited NT1.3 has I⁴=0; NT1.4 requires strictly regular weights. A correct source for the actual coefficient system could close this gate. Ramification was already excluded by standing assumptions.

gaps.title: Orientation and coherent patching duality
gaps.detail: For real places retain orientation coefficients or prove a Hecke-equivariant untwisting after localization. E65 does not establish failure of every localized self-duality. E39 also requires natural finite-level duality maps over one fixed ultrafilter and compatibility before inverse limits.

gaps.title: Residual image-field convention
gaps.detail: E42 is rejected because its counterexample violates the standing splitting coefficient-field assumption. Separate the minimal projective-image field from the chosen coefficient field before supplying a nonvacuous level-raising-prime theorem. No proposed ℓ≥7 repair is certified.

gaps.title: Remaining definition interfaces
gaps.detail: 33 definition/construction items still lack supplier-derived API outlines and three meaningful acceptance tests. The 26 added interfaces are planning sketches with named consumers, not compiled Lean. No suggested Lean deliverable or new planet packet is authorized by this review issue; those belong to the downstream design/blueprint jobs.
